ab.c.p: The result is signed on the phone. Its QR code lets anyone check it on another phone, offline, by re-running the same grading on the same measurements.
ab.i.p: The phone measures each visible onion: size in millimetres against a calibration sheet, and the share of its visible surface with blackening, rot, sunburn, spots, sprouting or peeled skin. Every number carries an uncertainty.
ab.l1: Only the visible surface is measured. Shake the tray and look again; hidden faces stay hidden.
ab.l2: The colour model has not yet been checked against graders on field photos. Accuracy numbers will appear only after that study.
ab.l3: White onions on a white sheet, piled onions, and patterned backgrounds are measured badly. Use the printed mat or a plain dark cloth and a single layer.
ab.l4: The dry root plate and neck can be mistaken for sunburn. Cuts are not measured by this version.
ab.l5: Weights are estimated from size with an assumed density until a kitchen-scale fit is loaded.
ab.l6: The receipt is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof. It cannot prove the photographed onions came from the sacks sold.
ab.l7: All procurement limits come from press reports; no official circular was found. The meaning of “URS” is unconfirmed.
ab.r.p: A rule pack turns measurements into Grade A, URS, Reject or “needs human check”. Anything within measuring error of a limit goes to a person, not to a coin flip. Packs are versioned and hashed, so a lot can be re-graded under any norm.
ab.src: Demo photos: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20254934, CC-BY 4.0. Code: open source. Built for Smart India Hackathon 2026, problem statement 26031.
ab.title: How it works & limits
bs.clean: Within every limit of the first bucket in this rule pack.
bs.disagree: The learned model thinks this bulb is unhealthy, but the colour model found no rot or blackening. It goes to a person.
bs.f.n: A contest moves this bulb to “needs human check” until an officer decides. Both steps stay on the record.
bs.frac.n: Area fractions of the visible surface, corrected for the curve of the bulb. Black ticks mark the nearest limit in this rule pack.
bs.label: Bulb {id}
bs.o.n: The AI verdict stays on record. Your change is added beside it and needs a new signed revision.
bs.title: Bulb {id}
cap.aside: {n} set aside (cut off by the frame edge or not onion-shaped).
cap.nocam: The camera could not be opened. Allow camera access for this site, or use Replay.
cap.ready.replay: Ready. Tap the shutter to measure this stored photo.
cert.bw: Shares by estimated weight. Grade A 95% interval: {a}–{b}%. {n} bulb-observations, tray-level intervals.
cert.noqr: Too many bulbs for one QR code; verify with the evidence file.
cert.scan: Scan with Parakh → Verify. Checks the signature and re-grades the lot on the scanning phone, offline.
cert.te: Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof: any change to this record breaks the signature or the re-grade. It does not prove the photos show the sacks that were sold.
cert.title: Receipt
dl.accept: The share of {bad} is below {p0}% with the chosen risk levels. Sequential test (SPRT) stopped.
dl.more: Not enough evidence yet. Sample about {k} more tray(s) from the drawn sacks.
dl.more0: Not enough evidence yet. Sample more trays from the drawn sacks.
dl.refer: {p}% of bulbs need a human check, more than this pack allows for an automatic decision.
dl.refermax: Reached the tray limit without a clear answer. An inspector decides.
dl.reject: The share of {bad} is above {p1}% with the chosen risk levels. Sequential test (SPRT) stopped.
fl.drift: Median bulb size per lot, mm (a steady slide can mean calibration drift)
fl.empty: No signed receipts on this phone yet.
fl.intro: Built from signed receipts only. Watch for a centre whose results drift, whose human overrides disagree with the model often, or that falls back to weak size calibration.
fl.server: With a sync server, every centre’s receipts and signed log heads land here. This build keeps everything on the phone.
fl.title: Fleet dashboard
gm.bright: Too bright. Avoid direct sun on the tray.
gm.bulbs: No onions found. Point the camera at the tray.
gm.dark: Too dark. Move to better light.
gm.glare: Glare on the onions. Tilt away from the light or shade the tray.
gm.level: Hold the phone flat, parallel to the table.
gm.sharp: Too blurry. Hold still or move a little further away.
gm.target: Keep the calibration sheet fully in view.
home.empty: No lots yet. Grade one with the camera, or load the demo lot: real market photos from Pune, replayed through the same pipeline.
home.h: Measure a lot. Issue a receipt anyone can check.
home.packs.s: Re-grade any lot under another norm.
home.verify.s: Scan a certificate QR. Works offline.
nl.draw.p: The farmer and the officer each type any 4 digits. Together they decide which {k} of {n} sacks, and which layer, get sampled. Neither side chooses alone, and anyone can recompute the draw later.
nl.farmer.s: Stored on this phone and printed on the receipt. Use a reference number if the seller prefers.
nl.replay.s: Replay feeds real stored photos through the same pipeline. The receipt is marked REPLAY.
nl.title: New lot
or.size: Size is wrong (checked with ring or caliper)
or.soil: Marked area is soil or shadow
pk.adopted: Lot now graded under this pack. Sign a new revision to issue it.
pk.intro: A rule pack is the rulebook: size window, defect limits, which buckets are bought. Packs are versioned and hashed. The same stored measurements can be re-graded under any pack, and each result can be verified on its own.
pk.nolots: Grade a lot first; then compare it under every pack here.
pk.title: Rule packs
pk.tt.n: Percent by estimated weight. Same measurements, same human actions; only the rulebook changes. Different pack hash, different result, both verifiable.
pk.use: Grade this lot under this pack
pk.warn: No official circular was found. Every pack here is built from press reports and marked so. Unknown limits are marked as assumptions in the pack notes.
r.border: {m} {v} is within measuring error of the {l} limit.
r.conf: The picture of this bulb is unclear (confidence {a}‰, needs {b}‰).
r.na: {m} is not measured by this model version.
res.audit.n: The AI verdicts are kept unchanged beside these actions. Signing creates a new revision; the earlier one stays valid and linked.
res.bayes.n: Bayesian view: Jeffreys credible interval on an effective sample of {n} bulbs (design effect {d}). Use it when there are only one or two trays.
res.ci.n: Intervals: {m}, resampling whole trays, never single bulbs. {n} bulb-observations from {tr} tray(s) × {lk} look(s). Looks re-observe the same onions, so they are not counted as new samples.
res.look2: Second look changed the non-Grade-A share by {d} percentage points (per tray). Hidden faces are why we shake and look again.
res.model: Perception: Tier-0 colour model, runs on this phone. Adjudication: rule pack {id}.
res.none: No onions have been measured in this lot yet.
res.nosheet: Some photos had no calibration sheet, so sizes come from the camera alone (about ±25%). Bulbs near a size limit go to a person. Use the printed mat or an A4 sheet for real grading.
res.tap: Tap a bulb for its reasons
res.title: Lot result
res.value.n: For {kg} kg declared, using the procurable share by weight and its interval. Indicative only, never an official price.
res.wilson: Wilson with design effect (fewer than 3 trays)
set.camh: Camera height if no sheet, mm
set.key.n: Created on this phone and cannot be copied out by the app. Clearing site data destroys it; receipts already issued stay verifiable.
set.lang.s: Translations other than English are machine drafts awaiting a native speaker’s proofread.
set.log.n: RFC 6962 Merkle log of every receipt hash. Publish the export daily: anyone holding an older signed tree head can prove later history was not rewritten.
set.rate.n: Default rate 2125 is from a press report of the July 2026 PSF procurement price (docs/SOURCES.md S5). Indicative only.
set.title: Settings & log
v.bad: This code is damaged, altered, or not a Parakh receipt. Nothing could be verified.
v.chain.na: Previous receipt from that device is not on this phone.
v.chain.s: Points to the previous receipt issued on that device.
v.fail.p: At least one check below failed. Do not rely on this receipt.
v.file: That file is not a Parakh evidence file.
v.head: Printed numbers match the re-grade
v.head.s: Headline on the receipt equals the recomputed one.
v.intro: Nothing is sent anywhere. This phone checks the signature, then re-runs the grading on the stored measurements with the named rule pack.
v.log.na: Not in this phone’s log (normal for a second phone). Check the centre’s published log.
v.nocam: Camera unavailable. Paste the code or open the evidence file instead.
v.ok.p: Signed by key {fp}. Re-graded here with the same result.
v.pack.u: Unknown pack hash: this phone cannot re-grade it.
v.regrade.s: {n} measurements → same bucket shares, intervals and decision.
v.title: Verify a receipt
